cases.prompt: We need a correlation id header on every response and we also want to measure handler execution time. Filter or interceptor?
expectations: Uses a servlet filter for the correlation id because it must cover non-controller requests and write the response header
Uses a HandlerInterceptor for handler timing because it needs the mapped HandlerMethod
Registers the interceptor through WebMvcConfigurer and orders the filter explicitly, noting the security chain runs at order -100

cases.prompt: Our @RestControllerAdvice handles IllegalStateException but the client still gets a 500 from the servlet container for exceptions thrown inside a filter.
expectations: States that controller advice is only consulted inside MVC dispatch
Moves handling into the filter or wraps the chain to rethrow inside dispatch
Confirms the advice is not swallowing 404s with a catch-all Exception handler

cases.prompt: Add a server-sent event stream to a Spring Boot 3.5 REST controller for ledger updates.
expectations: Registers onTimeout, onError, and completion handlers and sends an initial event to flush proxy buffers
States the connection cost and the proxy heartbeat requirement rather than assuming thread-per-client

cases.prompt: Clients get 406 when calling our JSON endpoint. Some callers send Accept: text/html. Fix it.
expectations: Declares produces on the mapping so the handler declares what it can write
Keeps favor-parameter false and refuses to add a format query parameter override
Explains the 406 from HttpMediaTypeNotAcceptableException and the 415 counterpart for Content-Type

cases.prompt: Our API returns an HTML 404 page for unknown paths instead of JSON, and someone noticed a config file is served statically.
expectations: Identifies the catch-all static resource mapping as the cause of both the HTML 404 and the exposed file
Sets spring.web.resources.add-mappings to false for the API service or narrows the static path pattern
Renders 404 through a scoped RestControllerAdvice as a problem document

cases.prompt: We are enabling virtual threads and our controller blocks on JDBC. What changes in DispatcherServlet and where is the new limit?
expectations: States controllers run on virtual threads and container thread pool properties stop applying
Names the datasource pool and any semaphore or queue as the real concurrency bound
Calls out carrier-thread pinning under synchronized on Java 21 and requires a measured before and after
